_readme: EXAMPLE BRD FRAGMENT — exists so the requirement pointers in examples/journeys/*.json
actually resolve, instead of the traceability being merely asserted.
A journey pointer is `<BRD id>#<RFC 6901 JSON Pointer>`, e.g. F101#/useCases/0/mainFlow/0
resolves to the first string of the first use case's main flow below. journey-runner.js
does NOT resolve or validate these — it copies the string into every finding it records.
Nothing in the harness will tell you a pointer is dangling, which is why
examples/validate-journeys.js resolves them against a BRD directory when you give it one.
The key set here mirrors the real BRD schema (id, title, modules, actors, useCases,
domainEntities, associations, microflows, pages, security, crossCuttingRequirements).
It is trimmed to the branches the example journeys point into; a real BRD is far larger.
NOTE ON THE SPEC: journey-proof.md illustrates the pointer format with `F007#/rules/3`.
That is illustrative only — the BRD schema has no `rules` key, so a pointer of that shape
does not resolve against a real BRD. Point at useCases / pages / security / microflows.
title: Purchase requests and supplier catalogue (example domain)

useCases.title: Submit a purchase request for approval
preconditions: At least one active supplier exists
postconditions: A PurchaseRequest exists in state Submitted, linked to the chosen supplier
An ApprovalRecord exists for that request
mainFlow: 6. User selects a supplier from the catalogue of active suppliers

7. User clicks Submit for approval; the system saves the request, links it to the selected supplier, sets state to Submitted, writes an ApprovalRecord and returns the user to the list with a confirmation
alternateFlows: 7a. No supplier selected — the system blocks submission and states which field is missing

useCases.title: Browse the integrated supplier catalogue
preconditions: The upstream catalogue service is reachable
postconditions: No data is written; the path is read-only
mainFlow: 2. System calls the upstream catalogue read model
4. User clicks Refresh to re-issue the same read-model call
alternateFlows: 3a. Zero entries returned — the system renders the designed empty state, not the framework default

domainEntities.name: CatalogueEntryReadModel
domainEntities.persistenceRationale: REST-fed read model; never written by this app. This is why J-CAT-01 declares no data or outcome rung.

buildComposition.emptyState: No purchase requests yet — create one to get started

actions.label: Submit for approval
actions.note: Must persist the request, set its supplier association, set Status to Submitted and write an ApprovalRecord. This is the pointer J-PR-01's submit step carries.

buildComposition.emptyState: The supplier catalogue returned no entries

security.model: Mendix role gates page access; the upstream service revalidates every call

crossCuttingRequirements: Every outbound call carries a trace header so the journey's span assertions can resolve
The catalogue path is read-only and must never write upstream
